1483631352.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Transverse section through the abdomen at the T12–L1 vertebral level, characterized by the presence of the epiploic foramen (foramen of Winslow) bounded anteriorly by the free margin of the lesser omentum (portal triad) and posteriorly by the inferior vena cava (IVC), along with the stomach, spleen, liver, and upper poles of both kidneys with suprarenal glands.
1483631352.keyConcept: A cross section at the T12–L1 level is defined by the epiploic foramen (omental bursa entrance), with the IVC posteriorly, the portal triad anteriorly, and both kidneys/adrenals flanking the aorta.

1813756422.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Paired strap-like muscle located on either side of the midline linea alba on the anterior abdominal wall, enclosed within the rectus sheath.
1813756422.keyConcept: The rectus abdominis is the primary vertical muscle of the anterior abdominal wall, separated from its contralateral partner by the linea alba and enclosed within the rectus sheath.

441987149.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Midline fibrous band running vertically down the anterior abdominal wall between the medial borders of the two rectus abdominis muscles, formed by the decussation of aponeuroses of the abdominal flat muscles.
441987149.keyConcept: The linea alba is an avascular fibrous raphe in the anterior midline of the abdomen formed by the fusion of the anterior and posterior rectus sheaths.

1024360141.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large parenchymal organ occupying the right hypochondrium and epigastrium, bounded peripherally by the diaphragm and body wall, and showing intrahepatic vascular channels.
1024360141.keyConcept: The liver is the largest solid abdominal organ, located primarily in the right hypochondrium and epigastrium, directly beneath the diaphragm.

1540828352.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Hollow sac-like structure with characteristic green biliary mucosal lining seated in the fossa for the gallbladder on the visceral surface of the liver.
1540828352.keyConcept: The gallbladder resides in the gallbladder fossa on the inferior/visceral surface of the liver, storing and concentrating bile delivered via the cystic duct.

1117110360.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Prominent hollow muscular digestive organ in the left upper quadrant/epigastrium with a large lumen, thick muscular walls, and folded mucosa, situated anterior to the lesser sac and pancreas.
1117110360.keyConcept: The stomach lies in the left hypochondrium, epigastrium, and umbilical regions, anterior to the omental bursa (lesser sac) and bed of the stomach.

2000724045.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Double layer of peritoneum extending from the liver (porta hepatis and fissure for ligamentum venosum) to the lesser curvature of the stomach and first part of the duodenum, forming the anterior wall of the lesser sac.
2000724045.keyConcept: The lesser omentum consists of the hepatogastric and hepatoduodenal ligaments, connecting the stomach's lesser curvature to the liver and enclosing the portal triad along its free margin.

610483593.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Peritoneal space (omental bursa) located posterior to the stomach and lesser omentum and anterior to the pancreas, communicating with the greater sac via the epiploic foramen.
610483593.keyConcept: The lesser sac (omental bursa) is a large peritoneal diverticulum situated behind the stomach and lesser omentum, allowing frictionless stomach distension.

1781483800.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large vascular lumen situated in the free margin of the lesser omentum (hepatoduodenal ligament) posterior to the hepatic artery and bile duct, and immediately anterior to the epiploic foramen.
1781483800.keyConcept: In the free border of the lesser omentum, the portal triad consists of the portal vein posteriorly, the bile duct anterolaterally (on the right), and the hepatic artery proper anteromedially (on the left).

131010966.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large retroperitoneal venous structure situated to the right of the vertebral body and aorta, directly forming the posterior boundary of the epiploic foramen.
131010966.keyConcept: The inferior vena cava (IVC) ascends retroperitoneally on the right side of the vertebral column and aorta, forming the definitive posterior boundary of the epiploic foramen of Winslow.

660339339.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large thick-walled arterial vessel positioned directly anterior to the lower thoracic/upper lumbar vertebral body (T12), situated between the crura of the diaphragm and medial to the IVC.
660339339.keyConcept: The abdominal aorta enters the abdomen through the aortic hiatus of the diaphragm at the T12 vertebral level, lying immediately anterior to the vertebral bodies and to the left of the IVC.

1760369511.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Bony vertebral body located in the posterior midline supporting the abdominal aorta and IVC anteriorly, corresponding to the T12 level at the epiploic foramen.
1760369511.keyConcept: The T12 vertebra forms the posterior skeletal landmark at the level of the aortic hiatus and epiploic foramen, flanked by the crura of the diaphragm.

532724809.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Musculotendinous band arising from the anterior and lateral aspects of the upper lumbar/lower thoracic vertebral bodies on the left side of the aorta, medial to the left suprarenal gland.
532724809.keyConcept: The left crus of the diaphragm arises from the upper two lumbar vertebral bodies and their intervertebral discs, lying to the left of the abdominal aorta.

824459077.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Prominent musculotendinous band arising from the upper lumbar vertebral bodies on the right side of the aorta, situated between the abdominal aorta and the IVC.
824459077.keyConcept: The right crus of the diaphragm is larger and longer than the left, arising from the bodies of L1–L3 and forming the muscular fibers of the esophageal hiatus.

2032773582.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Retroperitoneal bean-shaped parenchymal organ showing renal cortex and pelvis on the left side of the abdominal cavity, situated medial to the spleen and lateral to the aorta/left crus.
2032773582.keyConcept: The left kidney lies slightly higher than the right kidney (T11/T12 to L2/L3) and is related anteriorly to the stomach, pancreas, spleen, jejunum, and colic flexure.

1841376849.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Retroperitoneal parenchymal organ displayed on the right side of the cross section, situated posterior to the liver and lateral to the inferior vena cava and right crus.
1841376849.keyConcept: The right kidney lies lower than the left kidney due to the bulk of the right lobe of the liver, and is related anteriorly to the liver, duodenum, and right colic flexure.

1572672940.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Solid lymphoid organ located posterolaterally in the left hypochondrium, related to ribs 9–11 and positioned lateral to the left kidney and posterior to the stomach.
1572672940.keyConcept: The spleen is a highly vascular lymphatic organ situated beneath the left dome of the diaphragm in the left hypochondrium, related to the 9th through 11th ribs.

1902291413.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Pyramidal-shaped yellowish glandular tissue located retroperitoneally at the upper and medial pole of the right kidney, positioned directly behind the IVC.
1902291413.keyConcept: The right suprarenal (adrenal) gland is pyramidal in shape, capping the superior pole of the right kidney and lying immediately posterior to the IVC and right lobe of the liver.

1177124711.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Semilunar/crescentic yellowish endocrine gland situated on the medial border of the upper pole of the left kidney, lateral to the left crus of the diaphragm.
1177124711.keyConcept: The left suprarenal (adrenal) gland is semilunar in shape, extending along the medial border of the left kidney from the upper pole toward the hilum, related anteriorly to the stomach and pancreas.

654582224.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Contrast radiographic examination (fluoroscopy/X-ray barium study) demonstrating opacification of the upper gastrointestinal tract including the stomach and duodenal cap via ingested barium contrast (barium meal).
654582224.keyConcept: A barium meal is an upper gastrointestinal radiographic examination utilizing swallowed oral barium sulfate to evaluate the anatomy and mucosal contour of the esophagus, stomach, and duodenum.
